To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

low threshold voltage-gate potassium (LTK) channel currents are larger in frequency-selective neurons of the nucleus laminaris than in neurons that do not encode sound location, and that LTK currents regulate the strength of inhibitory synapses onto the frequency-selective neurons.

low threshold voltage-gate potassium (LTK) currents are larger in neurons of the nucleus laminaris that encode high frequency sounds and that the LTK currents regulate the amplitude and kinetics of inhibitory postsynaptically potentials in these neurons.

low threshold voltage-gate K+ channels (LTK channels) regulate inhibitory synaptic strength and the timing of inhibitory postsynaptics potentials (IPSP) in neurons of the avian nucleus laminaris (a nucleus that is important for the computation of sound localization).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular mechanisms of the auditory system and the role of the nucleus laminaris in the localization of sound.
the role of LTK channels and their interaction with inhibitory synapses in the development of the tonotopic organization of the nucleus laminaris in the avian auditory system.
the cellular and synaptic mechanisms that control the timing of action potential generation in neurons of the avian nucleus laminaris.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LTK currents are involved in the regulation of the strength of inhibitory synaptic inputs in ITD-codig neurons across their frequency axis.
LTK channels and synaptic inhibition interact in complex ways in NL neurons to control the threshold for action potential generation.
LTK channels in NL neurons are not only important in setting the threshold and timing of the action potential generation, but also in regulating the strength of inhibitory synaptic input.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LTK current plays a key role in shaping the membrane potential and action potential generation by regulating inhibitory synaptic inputs in ITD-codin NL neurons.
, in the NL of the chicken, low threshold voltage-gates are critical for shaping synaptic inhibition, and this is especially important at middle and high frequencies.
the interplay between LTK currents, depolarizing inhibition, and the frequency tuning of NL neurons is critical for the accurate encoding of ITD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LTK channels are critical for the precise tuning of the threshold and timing of the action potential generation in ITD-coders.
the LTK channels play an important role in shaping the response of NL neurons to inhibitory synaptic input, especially in the middle and high frequency regions.
LTK currents are critical for the regulation of inhibitory synaptic transmission and that the effects of LTKs are different in neurons of different frequency tuning.
